name: Kailasanathar Temple
description: Pallava-era Shiva temple in Kanchipuram, known for its ring of small shrines and rich Shaiva sculpture.
history: Built by the Pallava king Rajasimha (Narasimhavarman II) and completed by his son Mahendravarman III.
architecture: Sandstone Dravidian temple with a ring of small shrines around the main sanctum.

name: Brihadeeswarar Temple
description: Grand Chola temple at Thanjavur dedicated to Shiva, part of the Great Living Chola Temples.
history: Commissioned by Rajaraja I and consecrated around 1010 CE.
architecture: Granite vimana about 66 m tall, with a large Nandi at the entrance. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
description: Temple complex in Madurai dedicated to Meenakshi and Sundareswarar, famed for its colourful gopurams.
history: An ancient shrine rebuilt and expanded under the Nayak rulers.
architecture: Four towering gopurams with stucco figures, and the Thousand-Pillar Hall.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: Sun temple designed as a colossal stone chariot on the Odisha coast.
history: Built by Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty.
architecture: Chariot form with 24 carved stone wheels and seven horses. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Khajuraho Temples
description: Group of Hindu and Jain temples celebrated for finely carved sandstone sculpture.
history: Built by the Chandela dynasty over roughly a century.
architecture: Nagara-style temples on high platforms. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

name: Virupaksha Temple, Hampi
description: Shiva temple on the Tungabhadra river, in continuous worship since early medieval times.
history: Worship here dates to about the 7th century; expanded under the Vijayanagara empire.
architecture: Dravidian temple with a nine-tier gopuram. Part of the Hampi UNESCO World Heritage Site.
